predictions.question: Does the context entail the conclusion 'Atharv is good at fixing things.'?
predictions.reasoning: Atharv is a resourceful engineer (he enjoys problem solving and values sustainability). As a resourceful engineer he either finds innovative solutions or is creative with resources; we know he finds innovative solutions, so this condition is satisfied regardless of creativity. Atharv improves designs, so from the exclusive-or rule he does NOT repurpose materials (because if he did both improve designs and repurpose materials the antecedent would be false). Because he doesn’t repurpose materials and the implication ‘repurposes → conserves resources’ gives no information when the antecedent is false, we cannot establish that he conserves resources; indeed we know he is not environmentally responsible, and since conserving resources would force him to be environmentally responsible, he definitely does NOT conserve resources. Now consider the two mutually exclusive options: reduce electronic waste OR develop new products (but not both). If Atharv were to develop new products, then from the earlier conditional he must do either repurposing materials or improving designs but not both; since he improves designs and does not repurpose materials, the antecedent is satisfied and developing new products would follow. However, developing new products and reducing electronic waste cannot both be true. Let’s test the scenario in which he develops new products: then he does NOT reduce electronic waste. The contrapositive of the last conditional says that if he does not reduce electronic waste, then he is not good at fixing things AND not creative with resources. That would make the conclusion false. Let’s test the other scenario: suppose instead he does reduce electronic waste (and therefore does NOT develop new products). This scenario is consistent with all the conditionals. In this case nothing prevents him from being good at fixing things; in fact the only relevant conditional is: (good at fixing ∨ creative with resources) → reduces electronic waste. Since he does reduce electronic waste, this implication is satisfied regardless of whether the antecedent is true or false. So in this branch he could be good at fixing things or not. However, the question is whether the context ENTAILS the conclusion, i.e., guarantees it true in every model. Because there exists a consistent model (the first branch) where he does NOT reduce electronic waste and hence is NOT good at fixing things, the conclusion is not guaranteed. Therefore the correct answer is uncertain.
